title: Agent-Based Modelling of Social-Ecological Systems: Achievements, Challenges, and a Way Forward
publisher: JASSS (Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation)

key_points.claim: Review of ABMs of social-ecological systems using the TRACE good-modelling-practice framework (development, testing, analysis).
key_points.evidence_quote: we used the TRACE framework, which encompasses elements of model development, testing and analysis.

key_points.claim: Two-part method: review of reviews/method papers plus a mini-review of specific ABM publications.
key_points.evidence_quote: Results of the mini-review of 29 publications.

key_points.claim: Major gap: showing models represent real systems well enough (validation/realism).
key_points.evidence_quote: only 11 publications mentioned a comparison of model output to observation and data, and a strong case for model realism was not presented in any of these models.

key_points.claim: Major gap: systematic, transparent model analysis so output is understood, not just observed.
key_points.evidence_quote: analysing the models in a systematic and transparent way so that model output is not only observed but also understood.

key_points.claim: Recommended remedies: participatory approaches, standard communication protocols, code sharing, and tools for design and analysis.
key_points.evidence_quote: strategies such as participatory approaches, standard protocols for communication, sharing of source code, and tools and strategies for model design and analysis.

key_points.claim: ABMs of SES are useful for representing organisms, humans and institutions but are complex and hard to parameterize and analyse.
key_points.evidence_quote: ABMs of SES are by their very nature complex. They are therefore difficult to parameterize and analyse, which can limit their usefulness.

reliability_notes: Full text fetched (peer-reviewed, JASSS 2017). The mini-review is small (29 publications) and focused on social-ecological ABMs, not all artificial societies. Quotes come from the abstract and the body. The page is about 100k characters, and I read only selected parts.
